experiment: Structural search Phase 1, family (a): on rung 2 resume-projection-integrity and rung 4 pure-result-replay, do the five authored catalog seeds and the accepted unguided I1 children of direct differ in blind judge quality by more than two pooled within-arm standard deviations on both tasks, with DIRECT not the sole winner and I1 not collapsed?
solutions: not recorded here: this file sits in the runtime agents can read; the operator passes each task's solution commit with --solution and the scan uses it
arms: one per evaluation: each evaluation runs through prepare.run_arm with its evaluation id as the arm, so summarize reports one arm per evaluation; evaluation ids depend on the environment manifest and are not known before the runs, so none is listed. Policies are joined to evaluations by scoring.join_scores through each run row's records directory

policies.unguided: unguided:<candidate_id>, one policy per accepted I1 child of direct

batches: one pool per task (scoring.pool_evaluations): one batch holding the final patch of every completed, uncontaminated evaluation of that task plus both anchors
scale: each clone scores 0-8, the sum of score.orc's four rubric criteria (root_cause, scope, generality, layering), each 0-2, averaged over the judges not excluded; an evaluation's value is its final clone's (summarize's run value)
primary_measure: the blind rubric mean per task and policy: the mean of summarize's run values over the policy's valued evaluations, computed by scoring.phase1_readout from results.json joined by scoring.join_scores
primary_note: empty: summarize measures are per arm, here per evaluation, so no summarize measure names a policy; summarize reads only judges, primary and secondary from a criterion and accepts empty lists. The primary measure and the rules below are applied by scoring.phase1_readout

separation.rule: a task is separated when the largest difference between two policy means exceeds tolerance_sd times the pooled within-arm SD, sqrt(sum((n-1) s^2) / sum(n-1)) over policies with two or more valued evaluations; with no such policy the pooled SD is unavailable and the task is not separated

direct_sole_winner: on a task, DIRECT's mean exceeds every other policy's mean by more than the separation threshold
decision: first rule that fires: fewer than two separated tasks -> within_tolerance; DIRECT the sole winner on every separated task -> direct_sole_winner; the driver readout's I1 collapsed is true -> collapsed (an unavailable collapse figure does not fire); otherwise separated and phase2_selected is true. Only separated selects Phase 2
reported: per task and policy: runs, mean, within-arm SD, hidden_mean, calls_mean, wall_clock_mean
per task: pooled SD, threshold, largest gap, separated, DIRECT's rank
unguided I1: episode outcomes, distinct skeletons, revisit rate, terminal-only share, allocation_distinct, collapsed (driver readout)
anchor scores per judge and judge agreement (summarize results.json)
hidden_acceptance: descriptive only: reported per policy, never a threshold, gate, rank or selection
known_differences: one batch per task holds up to 18 clones (10 catalog evaluations, up to 6 children, 2 anchors), above the ten-clone batches of earlier experiments
unguided children may have one valued evaluation per task: their means count in the largest gap but contribute nothing to the pooled SD
a pooled SD of 0 makes any difference of means a separation
model_policy: no call uses a Fable model (owner, 2026-10-15): arms, mutators, judges and in-process subagents run behind the shims' model guard
